sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Describe your morning: when you get up, who you call, and what you look forward to.
items: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Separable verbs split in main clauses; reflexive verbs need a pronoun that points back to the subject.

blocks.text: Separable verbs carry a prefix that moves to the end of a main clause: aufstehen → Ich stehe um sieben auf. In a subordinate clause the prefix stays attached: …, weil ich um sieben aufstehe.

Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that refers back to the subject: ich freue mich, du freust dich, er freut sich. Some verbs are truly reflexive (sich beeilen), while others simply use a reflexive pronoun in certain meanings (sich vorstellen = to introduce oneself).

blocks.title: Two patterns, one sentence
blocks.text: Both can appear together: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende, weil ich dann ausschlafen kann.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.

items: In a main clause the separable prefix goes to the very end.
Reflexive pronouns in the accusative are mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich.
Some verbs take a dative reflexive pronoun: ich helfe mir, ich merke mir.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Listen once, then read the example aloud.

items.example: Ich stehe am Wochenende spät auf.
items.exampleEn: I get up late at the weekend.

items.example: Ich rufe dich heute Abend an.
items.exampleEn: I will call you this evening.

items.example: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
items.exampleEn: I am looking forward to the weekend.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
items.en: I am looking forward to the weekend.
items.note: The reflexive pronoun mich refers back to ich.

items.de: Sie ruft ihre Schwester jeden Tag an.
items.en: She calls her sister every day.
items.note: The prefix an moves to the end.

items.de: Wir beeilen uns, weil der Zug gleich fährt.
items.en: We are hurrying because the train leaves soon.
items.note: In the subordinate clause, the reflexive pronoun stays inside.
In a question the reflexive pronoun follows the subject.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The eu sounds like “oy”: zikh FROY-en.

blocks.text: “Freust du dich auf das Wochenende?” is a natural Friday question in German offices. The answer often includes a separable verb: “Ja, ich schlafe erst mal aus.”
Reflexive verbs are more common in German than in English. Phrases such as “sich beeilen” and “sich ausruhen” are everyday language, not formal or unusual.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: Two friends plan the weekend by phone.

lines.speaker: Jan
lines.en: What are you doing at the weekend?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.de: Ich stehe erst spät auf und rufe meine Eltern an.
lines.en: I will get up late and call my parents.

lines.speaker: Jan
lines.de: Freust du dich auf den Sonntag?
lines.en: Are you looking forward to Sunday?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.de: Ja, ich interessiere mich für das Konzert im Park.
lines.en: Yes, I am interested in the concert in the park.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Separable and reflexive verbs
sections.lede: Separable prefixes travel to the end; reflexive pronouns follow the subject.

rows: prefix stays attached in a subordinate clause

blocks.text: Common separable prefixes include auf-, an-, ein-, aus-, mit- and zu-. The meaning often changes with the prefix, so learn the verb as a pair.

sections.tip: If a verb has a stressed prefix, it is probably separable. Listen for the stress: AUFstehen, ANrufen.

exercises.explanation: The ich form is ich freue mich.
The du form is interessierst, and the reflexive pronoun is dich.
The prefix auf belongs at the end of the main clause.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.
sections.speaker: Ein Gespräch unter Freunden

script.speaker: Tom
script.de: Freust du dich auf den Urlaub?
script.en: Are you looking forward to the holiday?

script.speaker: Eva
script.de: Ja, ich freue mich sehr. Ich stehe dann nicht früh auf.
script.en: Yes, I am really looking forward to it. I won’t get up early then.

script.speaker: Tom
script.en: And what will you do there?

script.speaker: Eva
script.de: Ich interessiere mich für Wandern, also gehe ich jeden Tag los.
script.en: I am interested in hiking, so I set off every day.

questions.prompt: How does Eva feel about the holiday?
options: She is looking forward to it

questions.explanation: She says “Ich interessiere mich für Wandern.”

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Say what you look forward to this week and what you do in the morning. Use one reflexive and one separable verb.

model.de: Ich freue mich auf Freitag. Ich stehe um sieben auf und rufe meine Mutter an.
model.en: I am looking forward to Friday. I get up at seven and call my mother.

tips: Use mich after ich and dich after du.
Put the separable prefix at the very end of the sentence.
Practise the pair as one chunk: ich freue mich auf …

sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.right: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
items.why: Sich freuen needs the reflexive pronoun mich.
The time phrase comes before the final prefix.
Sich interessieren is reflexive in German.
